Main.AnnounceOnLan: Show this Mac on the local network
Main.AnnounceOnLan.Windows: Show this PC on the local network
Main.AnnounceOnLanTip: Lets NexaDesk on the same local network list this Mac for a direct connection. Connecting still needs a one-time code or pairing.
Main.AnnounceOnLanTip.Windows: Lets NexaDesk on the same local network list this PC for a direct connection. Connecting still needs a one-time code or pairing.
Main.MenuBarNote: Closing this window leaves NexaDesk running in the menu bar: remote control, connection prompts and the banner at the top keep working. Choose Quit from the menu bar to stop it.
Main.MenuBarNote.Windows: Closing this window leaves NexaDesk running in the notification area: remote control, connection prompts and the banner at the top keep working. To stop it, right-click the NexaDesk icon there and choose Quit NexaDesk.
Main.AdvancedHelp: You can connect without a server: directly on the same local network, and across networks with Tailscale on both devices, which does hole punching and falls back to a relay when that fails. You need a self-hosted signaling server only if you cannot use Tailscale and want to connect by 9-digit device ID (see docs/DEPLOY.md to deploy one).
Main.SecretHint: A signaling server always needs its key. Enter the one its owner gave you.
Main.SecretNotKept: The key could not be kept in the Keychain: {0}
Main.ModeNone: No server (addresses, the LAN and Tailscale only)
Main.ModePublished: A published server (pick one from the project's list on GitHub)
Main.ServerListCount: {0} published. The one you pick is used at once. The keys in this list are public.
Main.ServerListEmpty: No servers are published right now, or the list could not be reached.
Main.ServerHint: Use the form wss://server[:port], for example wss://signal.example.com
Main.ServerNotUsed: Not used (Tailscale is recommended across networks)
LoginItem.Enabled: Opens NexaDesk when you log in to macOS (you still turn on remote control yourself)
LoginItem.Enabled.Windows: Opens NexaDesk in the notification area when you sign in to Windows, with remote control on

LoginItem.RequiresApproval.Windows: Switched off in Settings → Apps → Startup: turn NexaDesk on there

LoginItem.CannotDisable: Could not turn off opening at login: {0}

Main.AllowBrowsersTip: The other person opens port 47801 of this Mac's address in a browser, with nothing to install. The one-time code and your confirmation still apply. Best kept to your LAN or Tailscale. Takes effect the next time you allow remote control.
Main.AllowBrowsersTip.Windows: The other person opens port 47801 of this PC's address in a browser, with nothing to install. The one-time code and your confirmation still apply. Best kept to your LAN or Tailscale. Takes effect the next time you allow remote control.
Main.AllowAgentsTip: AI agents (such as Claude through NexaDesk's MCP server) may ask to see and control this Mac. Each one is still put to you with its own dialog, and the banner shows that it is an AI. Applies at once.
Main.AllowAgentsTip.Windows: AI agents (such as Claude through NexaDesk's MCP server) may ask to see and control this PC. Each one is still put to you with its own dialog, and the banner shows that it is an AI. Applies at once.
Main.Mcp: AI agents (MCP): let an AI on this Mac control other computers
Main.Mcp.Windows: AI agents (MCP): let an AI on this PC control other computers
Main.McpHelp: NexaDesk comes with an MCP server, nexa-mcp. Add it to an AI app (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop and others) and the AI can connect to another computer running NexaDesk, see its screen and use its keyboard and mouse. The person there is asked first and sees that an AI is connected.
Main.McpClaude: Claude Code: run in a terminal
Main.McpJson: Apps configured with JSON (Claude Desktop and others)
Main.McpMissing: nexa-mcp is not next to this app (a development build): build it with cargo build -p nexa-mcp --release.
Main.McpOtherWay: For an AI to control this Mac, tick “Allow AI agents to connect” above.
Main.McpOtherWay.Windows: For an AI to control this PC, tick “Allow AI agents to connect” above.
App.ViewerNotYet: Connecting to other computers from Windows comes in a later version. Other devices can already connect to this PC.
Updates.NotInstalled: Updates come with the packaged app
Updates.Ready: Version {0} is ready: restarting ends remote sessions
Host.PairedNeedsHosting: Turn on remote control to see the devices paired with this computer.
